en.r: Mesa Verde National Park is a national park in Colorado, United States. It covers 212 km² and has been protected since 1906. It is managed by the U.S. National Park Service. en.h: Created on 29 June 1906 by Theodore Roosevelt, it was the first national park set aside for human culture. Ancestral Puebloans lived here from about 550 to 1300 and built villages beneath the cliffs. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978.
en.ff: Mesas of piñon pine and juniper cut by canyons; mule deer, wild turkeys and golden eagles.

pt.r: O Castlewood Canyon State Park é um parque estadual no Colorado, nos Estados Unidos. Tem 3,7 km² e está protegido desde 1964, sob gestão do governo estadual. Na classificação da IUCN, é uma paisagem protegida, onde natureza e uso humano tradicional convivem.
pt.h: Parque de 2.136 acres perto de Franktown, Colorado, na ponta norte da Black Forest, de 1.890 a 2.010 m. Guarda os restos da barragem de Castlewood, que se rompeu em 1933 e mandou uma onda de 5 m até o centro de Denver, e a histórica ponte Cherry Creek.
pt.ff: Geologia incomum com rochas de capeamento; coiotes, coelhos, raposas-vermelhas, ursos-negros e veados-mula.

en.r: Castlewood Canyon State Park is a state park in Colorado, United States. It covers 3.7 km² and has been protected since 1964. It is managed by the state government. Under the IUCN system it is a protected landscape, where nature and traditional human use coexist.
en.h: A 2,136-acre park near Franktown, Colorado, at the northern tip of the Black Forest, at 6,200 to 6,600 feet. It keeps the remains of Castlewood Canyon Dam, which burst in 1933 and sent a 15-foot wave to downtown Denver, and the historic Cherry Creek Bridge.
en.ff: Unusual caprock geology; coyotes, cottontails, red foxes, black bears and mule deer.

en.r: Cânion Negro de Gunnison National Park is a national park in Colorado, United States. It covers 124 km² and has been protected since 1999. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: It became a national monument on 2 March 1933 and a national park on 21 October 1999, when the Gunnison Gorge National Conservation Area was also created.
en.ff: The Gunnison River carved a narrow, deep canyon with dark rock walls up to 830 m high; some stretches get only minutes of sunlight a day. The Painted Wall is Colorado's tallest cliff. Peregrine falcons nest on the walls.

en.r: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve is a national park and preserve in Colorado, United States. It covers 344 km² and has been protected since 2004. Under the IUCN system it is a protected landscape, where nature and traditional human use coexist.
en.h: Herbert Hoover created the national monument on 17 March 1932. It was expanded and redesignated a national park and preserve on 13 September 2004.
en.ff: The tallest dunes in North America, up to 230 m, at the foot of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. The park runs from wetlands and grasslands to forest and alpine tundra above 4,000 m. In spring Medano Creek flows in surges along the base of the dunes.

en.r: Montanhas Rochosas National Park is a national park in Colorado, United States. It covers 1,076 km² and has been protected since 1915. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.

pt.r: A Black Ridge Canyons Wilderness é uma área selvagem nos Estados Unidos. Tem 305 km² e está protegida desde 2000, sob gestão do Escritório de Gestão de Terras dos EUA (BLM). Na classificação da IUCN, é uma área silvestre: um grande espaço pouco alterado, sem infraestrutura permanente.
pt.h: Área selvagem no oeste do Colorado, com uma pequena parte no leste de Utah, no árido Planalto do Colorado, 24 km a oeste de Grand Junction. A crista Black Ridge, de leste a oeste, é cortada por sete grandes sistemas de cânions que descem ao rio Colorado no Ruby Canyon. A altitude vai de 1.400 a 2.070 metros, e os cânions, de até 300 metros de profundidade, têm agulhas, janelas de pedra, grandes alcovas e verniz do deserto em falésias vermelhas.
pt.ff: O extrato não descreve fauna nem flora; o destaque são os cânions de rocha vermelha.

en.r: Black Ridge Canyons Wilderness is a wilderness area in the United States. It covers 305 km² and has been protected since 2000. It is managed by the Bureau of Land Management. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: A wilderness in western Colorado, with a small part in eastern Utah, on the arid Colorado Plateau about 15 miles west of Grand Junction. The east-west Black Ridge is cut by seven major canyon systems draining to the Colorado River in Ruby Canyon. Elevations range from 4,700 to 6,800 feet (1,400-2,070 m), and the canyons, up to almost 1,000 feet deep, hold spires, windows, giant alcoves and desert varnish on red rock cliffs.
en.ff: The extract does not describe wildlife or plants; the highlight is the red rock canyons.

es.ff: El extracto no describe fauna ni flora; lo destacado son los cañones de roca roja.

en.ff: It holds cutthroat, rainbow and brown trout and northern pike, and is famous for its kokanee salmon in the stretch called the Dream Stream.

en.r: Golden Gate Canyon State Park is a state park in Colorado, United States. It covers 32.4 km² and has been protected since 1960. It is managed by the state government.
en.h: A 49 km² Front Range state park in Gilpin and Jefferson counties, northwest of Golden, Colorado, established in 1960. It recorded over a million visits in 2019. Wetland and riparian communities line Ralston, Nott and Deer creeks.
en.ff: Forests hold ponderosa pine, Rocky Mountain juniper, Douglas fir and aspen. Wildlife includes mule deer, elk, black bear, mountain lion and Abert's squirrel, and moose are increasing. Birds include Steller's jay, Clark's nutcracker and mountain bluebird.

en.h: A 122,797-acre (497 km2) wilderness in the San Isabel and White River national forests of Colorado, near Leadville, Vail and Eagle. Established in 1980, it has 164 miles (264 km) of trails and is named for its highest peak, 14,005-foot (4,269 m) Mount of the Holy Cross. en.h: A Colorado state park around John Martin Reservoir, the state's second-largest body of water by capacity, formed by a dam 36 m high and 4.2 km long. The climate is cold semi-arid; in 2019 the dam recorded 46.1 °C, the highest reliably measured temperature in Colorado.
en.ff: It is a prime birdwatching spot: Bent County has over 400 recorded bird species. In 2022 thirty black-footed ferrets were released into a prairie dog colony in a nearby preserve.

en.ff: Moose are the park's claim to fame: North Park is considered Colorado's moose viewing capital, with over 600 moose year-round. There are also bighorn sheep, black bears, mule deer and elk.

en.r: Great Sand Dunes National Park is a national park in Colorado, United States. It covers 425 km² and has been protected since 2004. It is managed by the U.S. National Park Service. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: Herbert Hoover created the national monument on 17 March 1932. It was expanded and redesignated a national park and preserve on 13 September 2004.
en.ff: The tallest dunes in North America, up to 230 m, at the foot of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. The park runs from wetlands and grasslands to forest and alpine tundra above 4,000 m. In spring Medano Creek flows in surges along the base of the dunes.
